entities.summary: Samoa is a sovereign nation in Polynesia, Oceania. Its capital is Apia. Official languages include Samoan, English. Government: Unitary parliamentary republic (matai-based suffrage until 1990). Population: approximately 0.2 million. Area: 2,842 km². Comprehensive index for Samoa covering Polynesian settlement (~1000 BCE, 'Cradle of Polynesia', Lapita people), Samoan Empire (Tu'i Manu'a dynasty, oral tradition claims 3000+ years), European contact (Jacob Roggeveen 1722), missionary arrival (John Williams LMS 1830), Tripartite Convention 1899 (Germany took Western Samoa, US took Eastern/American Samoa), German Samoa (1900-1914), New Zealand mandate (1914-1962), Mau movement (non-violent independence, Lauaki Namulau'ulu, Black Saturday 1929), independence 1962 (first Pacific island nation), fa'a Samoa (Samoan Way), 2011 International Date Line switch.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Samoa's independence in 1962 marked a significant milestone for Pacific island nations, paving the way for other self-governance movements. With a population of approximately 0.2 million, its impact on regional politics and global decolonization efforts is notable.
